messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Polychoric correlations
parts: I wish to compute polychoric correlations between 17 items using lavCor. I am able to get the following results but I am also getting error messages. Can the results be trusted given the error messages?

Those are not error messages.  Those are just warnings, letting you know that you have empty cells in some bivariate tables, so the estimates of tetrachoric correlations were estimated by replacing those zeros with 0.5 (see the zero.add argument in the ?lavaan help page).  If you want more information, this article discusses the difficulty of estimating polychorics with empty cells and evaluated some correction methods:

http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10705511.2011.557339

Judging from her conclusions, you can probably trust your estimates because her recommendations are lavaan's defaults for zero.add.

Terry

messages.author: b8fd92e5e3662745
messages.subject: Re: Polychoric correlations
parts:
Just a quick note to follow-up on what Terry just said: from these
warnings, it looks like B4 and D4 tend to have these problematic
cells. If your model does not fall apart without them, you can try a
sensitivity analysis to see if the main results stay if you omit them.

Counterintuitively, if your correlation between the underlying normals
is very strong, you may be more likely to get empty cells. Most of the
cases will go to the cells on the diagonal, or near it, while the
cells at the far extreme across the other diagonal that have high
Mahalanobis distance from the center will have very low probabilities,
and likely zero counts in a sample. I hope I explain this well, I can
try to find a picture to make my point better :).
